items.title: ED is not super cop: Karnataka High Court quashes money laundering probe against Congress leader
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently quashed an Enforcement Directorate (ED) money laundering investigation naming Congress leader KY Nanje Gowda, stating that the agency was not a 'super cop' to investigate every case. [YB Ashwathanarayan v. Union of India] . Karnataka High Court ED is not a super cop to investigate anything and everything which comes into its notice. Justice MI Arun said that the ED could only prosecute as long as a foundational criminal offence is pending. "The power of the ED is derivative and not original. It cannot initiate an investigation suo motu based on a standalone suspicion of money laundering. If there is no existence of the predicate offence, then in that event, proceedings under PMLA cannot exist; meaning even when the predicate offence is terminated in favour of the accused therein, the proceedings under PMLA cannot continue." The Court further emphasised on the separation of powers between organs of government to outline the authority of the ED under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). items.summary: The third edition of Bengaluru ADR Week will be held from November 13 to 15, 2026, with judges, senior advocates and arbitration practitioners from India and abroad expected to participate in the three-day conference. Former Supreme Court judges Justices RV Raveendran, L Nageswara Rao, S Ravindra Bhat and Abhay S Oka will be among the prominent participants. The conference will feature discussions on the growing role of artificial intelligence in arbitration, the expanding scope of alternative dispute resolution (ADR), institutional independence, arbitral appointments and ethical standards. items.title: Prakash Raj meets Kalady Uni students, says he will join their hunger strike if needed
items.summary: In solidarity with the protesting students of Keralam’s Kalady Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, actor Praksh Raj said that he would join their hunger strike if they are not allowed to write exams. The actor met with the 16 suspended students on Saturday, November 7, and said that the state government and the higher education minister, Roji M John, must take accountability for the future of the students. "I have come here for a protest, but I promise that if this continues, I will come and sit with them here. I have no problem. I can stop everything and come and sit here," Prakash Raj said. The actor questioned how long the university would continue suppressing dissent among young students. "What is this anarchy, dictatorial behaviour of the university or the education minister of this state? How long will everybody become like Modi and the Central government to stop youngsters from protesting and asking questions?" he asked. "This generation is not Savarkar's to write sorry petitions. items.title: NMC founder BR Shetty held liable for $5.4 billion healthcare fraud by Abu Dhabi court
items.summary: The Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) Court has held NMC Healthcare founder BR Shetty and former Chief Executive Officer Prasanth Manghat liable for fraudulent and wrongful trading in connection with a massive financial fraud that led to the collapse of the healthcare group in 2020. Justice Sir Andrew Smith of the ADGM Court of First Instance held that both Shetty and Manghat had knowingly participated in a fraudulent scheme involving the misappropriation of company funds, concealment of borrowings and manipulation of financial statements. The Court identified $5.397 billion as the starting point for assessing the financial contributions that the two would be required to make towards the company's assets. The November 5 judgment revealed that over 500 transfers were made into Shetty's personal bank accounts. These transfers totalled AED 4.18 billion, with net payments of approximately AED 2.6 billion after accounting for funds returned to the group. The case arose from the collapse of NMC Health, which Shetty founded in Abu Dhabi in 1975.
